blockSrc: Agronomy Report 1/2026 Table 14 (by year of planting)
summary: FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026) yield 20.20 t/ha (Agro Table 14); every planting except P12 rose 9–100%+, but the printed FY2024/25 average of 21.25 t/ha cannot be reproduced from the block rows, so the reported 4.9% fall is doubtful.
May–Dec 2025 (8 months): 18,965.64 t FFB, 12.90 t/ha, 5% below the 13.58 budget and above 12.66 t/ha a year earlier (PA).

Ex-estate cost RM393.09/t vs a like-for-like budget of RM289.08 (May–Dec 2025), about 36% over; PA reports '23% below' only because its RM508.38 budget includes RM219.30 dispatch & storage with no actual.
Upkeep RM252.66/t vs RM164.22: roads & bridges RM75.62/t vs RM22.38 (road raising and laterite) and fertiliser over-applied from carry-over stock (PA).
Stand is thin: 132 SPH estate average, P18–P20 down 26–31% since 2021; only 5,986 of 11,743 planned supply palms planted by Apr 2026 and many died from flooding (Agro).

issues.title: Cost 'below budget' only because budget includes dispatch
issues.detail: PA Table 17(b) / 9.1 / 12.11: ex-estate RM393.09/t is '23% below' budget RM508.38/t. The budget includes Dispatch and Storage RM219.30/t (IDR913,719/t) while actual shows '-'. Excluding it, budget is RM289.08/t (69.78 + 164.22 + 55.08) and actual is about 36% over budget; upkeep alone is RM252.66 vs 164.22 (+54%).

issues.title: Agro FY2024/25 estate yield 21.25 t/ha does not match its own block rows
issues.detail: Agro Table 14: the printed FY2024/25 estate average is 21.25 t/ha, but the block rows weighted by the 1,470.18 ha shown give 18.38 t/ha (the FY2025/26 rows give 20.20, matching the printed figure). Even the rows' implied production (27,019 t) over PA Table 16's FY2024/25 mature area of 1,344.1 ha gives only 20.10 t/ha. So the printed 4.9% decline is not supported by the table itself; Agro 7.1 also asks the estate to verify the average.

issues.title: Palm supply: planned vs planted
issues.detail: Agro 2.12 says 11,743 palms were planted over 82.12 ha in FY2025/26. Agro Table 4 shows 82.12 ha / 11,743 palms is the plan (Rencana FY25-26); actual planted May 2025 to Apr 2026 is 41.84 ha / 5,986 palms.

issues.title: Harvesting cost budget: RM63.91 vs RM55.08
issues.detail: PA Table 15(b) and 7.8: harvest & collection RM68.66/t vs budget RM63.91 (IDR218,058, budget amount / budget crop 19,960 t, at IDR3,412). PA Table 17: RM68.65 vs RM55.08 (IDR229,496, same budget amount / actual crop 18,965.64 t, at IDR4,166.48). 7.8 says 25% over; IDR286,048 vs 218,058 is 31% over (vs 229,496 it is 25%). Table 15(a) labels per-tonne columns 'TODATE/HA'. Tables 8, 9 and 15(a)/(b) label the budget column 'Year Budget' and the text calls it the 'annual budget', yet 15(a) budget/t = IDR4,352,532,607 / 19,960.40 t (8-month budget crop) and Table 17 uses the same amounts as 'Budget 8M'.

issues.title: Two exchange rates mixed in PA cost tables
issues.detail: PA Tables 7, 9 and 15(b) budgets use RM1 = IDR3,412; actuals in Tables 9, 15(b) and 17 use IDR4,166.48; Table 7 general charges uses 3,412 for actual too (RM1,038.61/ha). Same IDR figures give different RM: harvesting IDR154,251 actual (RM37.02) is 19% over IDR129,105 budget, yet RM37.02 is below the RM37.84 budget.

issues.title: Selective weeding budget misquoted
issues.detail: PA 6.1.4.10: actual IDR518,459 (RM124.44)/ha 'is 18% higher than the annual budget of IDR518,459 (RM128.44)'. Table 8 budget is IDR438,246/ha (Table 9 RM128); the RM figures show actual below budget.

issues.title: Circle spraying hectares misquoted
issues.detail: PA 6.1.3.1 says circle spraying was completed on 1,703.49 ha (1.9 rounds). Table 10 grand total completed is 2,819.92 ha (64%); 1,703.49 ha is Division 4's programmed area.

issues.title: Manuring programme total off by 6.45 mt
issues.detail: PA Table 12 full-year programme lines add to 3,315.11 mt (as Agro Table 5), but the printed total is 3,308.66 mt (difference = urea 6.45). PA 6.2.1 describes the 8-month work as 'first half / past six months'. Agro Table 5 FY total applied 3,968.15 mt (120%).

issues.title: PA harvesting interval table misaligned
issues.detail: PA Table 14: hectare values are shifted against block names from HJ43-12A1 onward (HJ43-12A1 shows 59.37 ha, the Division 2 sub-total; it is 12.05 ha in Table 3), all year-of-planting entries read 2012 or 2013, and HK44-13A1 appears twice.

issues.title: Immature planting years inconsistent
issues.detail: PA Table 3 immature rows by planting year give 2022 5.64 ha, 2023 31.21, 2024 28.74, 2025 12.32 (e.g. HF39-23A1 dated 2022, HF41-24B1 dated 2023, HF36-25B1 dated 2024), while PA Table 2 and Agro Table 1 give 0.42, 31.92, 30.60, 14.97 ha. Totals agree (129.78 ha).

issues.title: Report labels and names
issues.detail: Agro cover page reads 'Agronomy Report 2/2025' (report no. 1-2026) and names Bpk Richard Frenky Sibuea as manager; PA 3.1 says he left and Bpk Lalu Suryandi took over in Sep 2025. PA summary header reads '(2-2025)' and PA 1.1 gives the previous visit as 'February 21st and 22nd, August 2025'. Agro 2.7 says immature is under 100 ha (2%) while its Table 1 shows 129.78 ha.

issues.title: General charges appendices: RM not converted, % and per-ha errors
issues.detail: PA Appendix 2 (RM) shows IDR-scale numbers (e.g. staff salary 151,710,797, total 1,662,146,818; true RM is 1,662,147 per Table 7) and '#DIV/0!' for water/electricity. PA text 5.4 says staff bonus 60%, ISPO 144% and repairs 65% over budget; Appendix 1 amounts give +160%, +244% and +165% (bonus IDR170.9m vs 65.6m). Appendix 1 budget IDR/ha for labour and office lines is understated (e.g. labour wages 286 vs IDR716,683,101 / 1,599.96 ha = 448; security 169 vs 264) though sub-totals (939, 1,027) are right.

issues.title: HG37-20A1 hectares differ
issues.detail: PA Table 3 gives HG37-20A1 as 23.57 ha (2,570 palms, 109 SPH); Agro Table 4 and Table 6 give 21.82 ha (2,320 palms, 106.30 SPH). The P2020 immature total is 51.87 ha in both reports.

issues.title: 2025 planting area: 16.65 ha in text vs 14.97 ha in tables
issues.detail: PA 11.2 says the 2025 planting (F36-25B1 and F37-25A1) covers 16.65 ha. PA Table 2 and Agro Table 1 give 2025 planting as 14.97 ha; PA Table 3 lists HF36-25B1 2.65 ha and HF37-25A1 3.61 ha (6.26 ha). The 16.65 ha also differs from the 16.72 ha immature increase in PA 2.2/11.1.

actions.item: Supply dead and vacant points (about 8,000 seedlings from Seluang nursery), esp. flooded 2025 planting
Re-census palms after supplying; verify the abnormal SPH drop in P18–P20
Restrict glyphosate to palm circles; use Triclopyr (Garlon) for Asystasia, Paraquat + Ally for Stenochlaena, sedges, VOP
Raise sprayer output from 3.5 to 5.0 ha/man-day
Keep harvesting intervals 10–15 days; enforce loose fruit collection; fill any harvester shortage before peak
Reduce internal transport; move FFB direct from platform to mill as lateriting progresses
Finish laterite surfacing of about 21 km raised road (about 30% of roads) within two financial years
Use idle Startrac mini tractors for mechanised infield collection; write off or sell unused vehicles
Submit complete manuring records; clarify HGFB and ZA stock left after 'completed' programmes
Apply fertiliser in weeded circles (not frond heaps) within two months of receipt; suspend in flooded areas
Improve compost: full coverage, no over-application or roadside dumping, priority to non-flooded areas; bands 1.5–2.0 m from young palms
Correct under-pruning (HG35, HL24, HL39, HK24) and over-pruning in young palms; stack fronds among four palms
Lower high water tables to 45–60 cm (desilt, clear blockages, maintain gates and weirs)
Quarterly rat census in every field; bait only at 10% damage
Merge small sub-blocks (esp. P17, P22) toward 40–60 ha and install clear block labels
Re-check reported estate average yield (FY2024/25 21.25 t/ha)
Anti-theft measures: no FFB left overnight on boundaries, patrols, stagger harvest days vs village plots

costDetail.src: PA Report 1/2026, section 9 Table 17(b); items from Tables 8, 15(a) and Appendix 1 (IDR amounts)
notes: Like-for-like budget: PA Table 17(b) prints ex-estate RM393.09/t actual vs RM508.38/t budget ('23% below'), but the budget includes Dispatch and Storage RM219.30/t (IDR913,719/t) while actual is '-' (nil). The budget shown here, RM289.08/t, is the sum of the three printed group budgets (69.78 + 164.22 + 55.08) without dispatch; on that basis actual is about 36% OVER budget. kpi.copBudget uses the same RM289.08.
Actual total RM393.09/t is as printed; the three printed group actuals add to RM393.08.

Table 17 converts IDR at 4,166.48 per RM for actual and budget alike, and divides budget amounts by ACTUAL FFB 18,965.64 t (e.g. upkeep budget IDR12,976,732,448 / 18,965.64 t = IDR684,223/t), not by the 8-month budget crop of 19,960.40 t.

All items are calc: IDR amount (Tables 8, 15(a), Appendix 1) / 4,166.48 / 18,965.64 t, the same basis as Table 17. They reproduce the printed group figures (upkeep 252.66 / 164.22; general charges 71.77 / 69.78; harvest 68.65 / 55.08). Harvest actuals equal the per-tonne figures printed in Table 15(b); Table 15(b) budgets (3.43, 37.84, 6.93, 14.68, 1.04 = RM63.91) use IDR3,412 and budget FFB, so they are not used here.

Upkeep has 18 lines and general charges 27 lines; the 13 largest by actual are shown in report order and the rest summed as Other (upkeep: supervision, pests & diseases, census, tools, other upkeep; general charges: 14 smaller lines).

General charges exclude depreciation (IDR4,574,597,800) and amortisation (IDR2,853,771,868), as the ex-estate cost does. Below the line Table 17(b) adds processing RM10.88/t (budget 13.15), head/regional office RM7.69 (7.97) and depreciation/amortisation RM94 (144): grand total RM506/t FFB vs RM674 budget (both budgets include the RM219.30 dispatch); RM2,505/t CPO vs RM2,061.
Inti division only (1,599.96 ha planted, 1,470.18 ha mature).

kb:
HARUAN ESTATE (INTI), PT Lifere Agro Kapuas (PT LAK), Kalimantan, UMB group. Fact pack from PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisor En Adnan Bin Mustafa, visit 5-6 February 2026, review period May 2025 to December 2025, 8 months of FY2025/26) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Agronomist Mr Chong Kuan Ming, visit 19 May 2026; previous visit 26 November 2025). Plantation Director Mr Tee Tong Heng; Senior Manager Bpk Deni Irawan; Estate Manager Bpk Lalu Suryandi (joined estate 25 Sep 2025, promoted from Senior Assistant Manager at Biawan; previous manager Bpk Richard Frenky Siboea/Sibuea left; the Agro cover still names him). Financial year runs May to April. PA money is in IDR with RM conversions; cost-of-production tables use RM1 = IDR4,166.48, several budget columns use IDR3,412. Figures are Inti division only unless stated.

AREA (PA Table 1, Dec 2025): mature 1,470.18 ha (+0.16 vs Jul 2025), immature 129.78 ha (+16.72, new rehabilitation), planted 1,599.96 ha. Building sites and roads 147.01 ha, vacant plantable 339.84 ha, vacant unplantable 213.57 ha. Title 2,300.38 ha (was 2,348.59). Mature by year (PA Table 2): 2012 357.42 ha, 2013 713.14, 2015 72.42, 2016 121.07, 2017 7.66, 2018 70.49, 2019 116.86, 2020 11.12. Immature: 2020 51.87, 2022 0.42, 2023 31.92, 2024 30.60, 2025 14.97. Prime age 1,271.71 ha; young 198.47 ha. Divisions (PA Table 3, mature): Div 1 236.74 ha (32,179 palms, 136 SPH), Div 2 59.37 ha (143 SPH), Div 3 606.24 ha (139 SPH), Div 4 567.83 ha (124 SPH); total mature 195,487 palms, 133 SPH; immature 16,490 palms, 127 SPH; estate 211,977 palms, 132 SPH.
AREA (Agro Table 1, as at April 2026): same 1,599.96 ha; 2020 immature corrected from 50.12 to 51.87 ha. Agro Table 2: 134 sub-blocks averaging 11.9 ha (P12 17 blocks avg 21.0 ha; P13 36 avg 19.8; P18-P19 under 6 ha; P23-P25 2.5-3.5 ha). Merge small blocks (esp. P17, P22) to 40-60 ha; block labels inadequate. Age profile chart: 0-3 yrs 78 ha (2%), 4-7 yrs 180 ha (10%), 8-19 yrs 1,342 ha (87%). No replanting for five years. P20 reaches maturity this year (PA: G37-G40-20A1, 51.87 ha, to be declared mature May 2026).

PALM DENSITY (Agro Table 3, SPH 2021 vs current): 2012 149 to 145; 2013 139 to 136; 2015 138; 2016 132; 2017 125 to 128; 2018 148 to 102 (-31.1%); 2019 135 to 95 (-29.6%); 2020 143 to 106 (-25.9%); 2022 102; 2023 143; 2024 140; 2025 143; total 141 to 132 (-6.4%). The P18-P20 drop is abnormal and must be verified. Blocks under 100 SPH in P13, P16, P18, P19, P20 need infilling. PA Table 3 very low stands: HK37-19C1 13 SPH, HF38-19A1 27, HD40-19A1 29, HK38-20A1 40, HD36-19A1 52, HG38-20A1 52, HD38-18A1 55, HK38-16B1 61. Supply records (Agro Table 4): plan FY25-26 82.12 ha / 11,743 palms; actually planted May 2025 to Apr 2026 41.84 ha / 5,986 palms. Agro text 2.12 describes 11,743 palms as planted. About 8,000 more seedlings needed, from Seluang nursery. Many supplied palms died from flooding.

STAFF AND LABOUR (PA, Dec 2025): Estate Manager, KTU (Muhammad Rusli) and 4 Assistant Managers; no Field Supervisor, mandores per division. Labour (covers Inti and Plasma, 2,559.05 ha planted, all on checkroll): 307 workers vs 359 required (short 52). Harvesting 167 vs 190 (harvester/carrier 143 vs 153, checker 8, FFB lorry 16 vs 29); P&D 2; manuring 27 vs 30; weeding 38 vs 35; pruning 8 vs 12; mandore 10; internal transport 2; general workers 53 vs 78 (general worker 17 vs 30, tractor driver 7 vs 19, gate security 13). Ratios: 1 worker per 8 ha; 1 harvester per 17 ha over 2,422.76 ha mature (Inti and Plasma); 90% of harvesters from Lombok.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Tables 6-7, May-Dec 2025, 1,599.96 ha): excluding depreciation and amortisation IDR5,671,244,943 = IDR3,544,617/ha (RM1,038.61/ha at IDR3,412) vs budget IDR3,446,114/ha (RM1,010), 3% over. Staff salary and related IDR1,575,178/ha (RM461.66) vs 1,477,381 (RM433.00), +7%. Office and related IDR1,375,034/ha (RM403.00) vs 1,027,076 (RM301.02), +34%. Over budget: staff bonus, BPJS Kesehatan +30%, accommodation +27%, ISPO (text 144%, appendix 244%), repairs (text 65%, appendix 165%). PA: acceptable.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Tables 8-9, 8 months, mature 1,470.18 ha): total IDR19.97 bn = IDR13,580,205/ha, RM3,259/ha vs year budget RM2,587/ha. Per ha (RM, actual vs budget): supervision 7 vs 27; selective spraying and lalang 124 vs 128; manuring total 1,734 vs 1,559 (material 1,616 vs 1,485; labour 56; contract 41; transport 21); composting 210 vs 233; P&D 2 vs 12; census 2; drains 31 vs 48; roads and bridges 976 vs 353 (338% of budget); soil/water 14 vs 17; supplying 83 vs 101; pruning 69 vs 93; tools 5; other 2.
Weeding (PA 6.1): 38 sprayers, 9-10 per division. Circle spraying (Table 10) programmed 4,410.54 ha (3 rounds), completed 2,819.92 ha, 1.9 rounds, 64%; average cost RM21.78/ha per round. Circles generally clean (blanket Paraquat + Ally) but Asystasia appearing; estate mixes Glyphosate with Starane, advised not to: glyphosate only in the circle, Triclopyr (Garlon) for Asystasia during interrow spraying. Productivity 3.5 ha/man-day, target 5.0; pay IDR192,500 (RM46.70)/day. Selective spraying (Table 11): 3,358.23 of 4,410.54 ha, 2.3 rounds, 79%; some fields only 1 round, delayed by harvester path mounding. Interrow: Triclopyr for soft grass; Paraquat + Ally for Stenochlaena/sedge/VOP every 2-3 months; train sprayers to avoid bare ground.
Manuring (PA Table 12, 8 months): programme to date 1,962.66 mt; applied 3,514.39 mt (179%), 106% of the full-year programme (printed 3,308.66 mt). Over-application from FY2024/25 carry-over Mix B (2,082.53 vs 1,187.90 mt) and NK Mixture (593.45 mt unprogrammed). Kieserite 50%, compound 62%. 27 workers, 20 bags per man-day at IDR8,000 (RM1.92), pay IDR160,000 (RM38.41); some use self-bought wheelbarrows; workers lent to Seluang. Cost RM1,734/ha, 136% of budget.
Composting (PA): RM210/ha vs 233; suggest a tracked carrier to place compost in harvester paths. P&D: rats only, IDR7,933 (RM1.90)/ha, 19% of budget. Pruning (Table 13): programme 3,171.90 ha (2 rounds), done 1,669.65 ha, 53% (Div 1 61%, Div 2 48%, Div 3 63%, Div 4 37%); first round done; some over-pruning in young mature; stack fronds among four palms; cost RM69.13/ha, 79% of budget. Roads: raising at IDR15,500 (RM3.72)/m; about 21 km raised road (about 30% of agricultural roads) still to be surfaced, within two financial years. Drains RM31.04/ha, 21% under budget, satisfactory. Soil and water conservation RM14.46/ha, 104% of budget: flap gate, bakau-wood weir, soil-filled bags; keep water 50-75 cm below ground.

HARVESTING (PA section 7): 143 harvesters, manual cut and carry, wheelbarrow to platform; lorry direct to Arowana mill where laterited; elsewhere small tractor or Badang (1.5-3.0 t) to collection centre, 40-50% of area. Intervals below 10 days (block averages 7-9 days, Table 14); rounds above the minimum 16 to date; PA wants 10-15 days. Cost (Table 15, per tonne FFB): supervision RM3.63; harvesting own FFB RM37.02 (IDR154,251, 19% over IDR129,105); infield loading RM11.37 (IDR47,364, double budget); internal transport RM15.81 (IDR65,882, 31% over); tools RM0.82; total RM68.66 (IDR286,048) vs RM63.91 (IDR218,058) in Table 15(b), RM55.08 (IDR229,496) in Table 17. PA: acceptable.
HARVESTING (Agro 4.1, Table 9): monthly intervals May 2025-Apr 2026 by division 6-13 days. At the May 2026 visit intervals slightly over 15 days (festivals). Bunch checks: P12-HL24 under 2% over-ripe; P13-HF35 8% over-ripe and 2% rotten; P13-HH40 under 2%; P15-HG38 8% over-ripe; P15-HK45 under 2%; P16-HK45 0%. Abundant loose fruit in HF35, oxidised loose fruit in HK24. Table 15: P12 harvesting rounds to April 2026 101% of 36 target (HG35 92%, HJ44 91%). Young mature: tantan busuk (rotten bunches) in P19 and P20; over-ripe and empty bunches at HK49-P19 platforms.

CROP AND YIELD (PA Table 16, May-Dec 2025, 1,470.18 ha): FFB 18,965.64 t vs budget 19,960.40 (-5%), 64% of annual budget 29,791.65 t; last year same period 17,023 t on 1,344.1 ha. Yield 12.90 t/ha vs 13.58 budget and 12.66 last year same period; annual budget 20.26 t/ha. CPO 3,829.16 t, OER 20.19% (budget 21.00%); kernel 627.76 t, KER 3.31% (4.00%). CPO 2.60 t/ha vs 2.85. PA expects the annual budget to be met.
YIELD (Agro Table 14, FY2024/25 vs FY2025/26, May-Apr): P12 26.87 to 24.21 (-9.9%); P13 18.48 to 20.08 (+8.7%); P15 14.69 to 25.75 (+75.3%); P16 12.64 to 16.63 (+31.6%); P17 23.74 to 30.22 (+27.3%); P18 9.23 to 12.14 (+31.5%); P19 6.65 to 13.36 (+100.9%); P20 2.96 to 18.33 (+519%); estate 21.25 to 20.20 (-4.9%). Agro asks the estate to verify the average: block rows weighted by the 1,470.18 ha give 18.38 for FY2024/25 (and 20.20 for FY2025/26, matching); over PA's FY2024/25 mature area of 1,344.1 ha the rows give 20.10, so the printed 21.25 and the 4.9% fall cannot be reproduced.
